messages.author: a28ce37a2d809bbf
messages.subject: Non-comformable array error from overlap()
parts:
Good morning,

   I have a large list of UDs (352 elements) that I would like to calculate overlap on, but I am running into an error:

Error in object[[1]]$PDF * object[[2]]$PDF : non-conformable arrays

When I looked at the dimension of the PDFs for each list element, I noticed they were all different, e,g.

> dim(UDList2[[1]][["PDF"]])
  x   y 
119 115 
> dim(UDList2[[2]][["PDF"]])
  x   y 
125 149 
> dim(UDList2[[3]][["PDF"]])
  x   y 
129 137

I suspect differing dimensions are responsible for throwing that error, but I couldn't locate the error in the github source code for the function (https://github.com/ctmm-initiative/ctmm/blob/master/R/overlap.R). If differing PDF dimensions for each fitted UD is what is causing the wrror, is there a way to standardize the dimensions of the PDFs so that I can calculate UD overlap? (Incidentally, I noticed that the functions calls for "aligned UDs." How does one ensure they are getting aligned UDs?) Alternatively, is there something else that could be causing the error?

Many thanks in advance,
Jenny Hansen

messages.author: 89513a910b665246
messages.subject: Re: Non-comformable array error from overlap()
parts:
Hi Jenny,


Chris might be able to answer to your question a bit more smoothly, but I'll give it a shot in the meantime.

I too have run into that same error. I was using lapply() to run akde() over my telemetry object (large list of 129 objects) -  you don't need to do this. I believe that using lapply() with akde() causes it to create a unique grid for each telemetry object. I got rid of lapply() and just ran akde() on my list of telemetry objects along with my list of fits (CTMM = ). By doing this the same grid was applied to all 129 telemetry objects and I was able to run the overlap() thereafter.

So don't do this:

AKDES <- lapply(1:length(telem.obj), function(d){akde(telem.obj[[d]], best.fit[[d]])})

Keep it simple and do this:

AKDES <- akde(telem.obj, best.fit)


Put simply, running akde() directly on a list automatically estimates akdes for all objects using the same grid.

Good luck!


- Teague

messages.subject: Re: Non-comformable array error from overlap()
parts:
Hi Jenny and Teague,

This is the correct answer, thanks.

The grid option is also now supported in newer versions of the package if you know a priori what grid you want to calculate everything on.

https://ctmm-initiative.github.io/ctmm/reference/akde.html

https://ctmm-initiative.github.io/ctmm/reference/overlap.html

Best,
Chris
